title: Quickstart Minima Bootpack and Runloop Heuristics (playbook)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, opinionated playbook for producing a 3- to 30-minute developer experience using the SDKs. The focus is on a tiny, low-friction "Minima Bootpack" (what we hand a new dev or integrator to get to first working call) plus a set of runloop heuristics to keep iteration fast without sacrificing production readiness.

Audience:
- SDK writers and docs engineers
- Solutions engineers running demos / POCs
- Developer advocates creating quickstarts and templates

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- 3-minute developer: run a single curl/Python example that returns a valid generation
- 15-minute integrator: wire example into a tiny web endpoint and see streaming responses
- 30-minute production smoke: add telemetry, CI smoke test, and per-route error handling
- Metrics: time-to-first-success (target < 5 min for 60% of trials), onboarding NPS > 60 in trials

Minima Bootpack contents (what we distribute):
- tiny repo skeleton (README, example.env, quickstart.py, quickstart.sh)
- single-file example per language (py, js, curl) with no deps beyond standard libs
- a minimal prompt + small recommended model (verified for latency/cost)
- an examples/ folder with two short apps: "hello-generation" and "chat-echo"
- a clearly named credential placeholder and short note about secrets (KMS note)

File: example.env (example contents)
- REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_live_XXX (note: use dev token in docs)
- REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
- SAMPLE_MODEL=redwood/minima-1b

3-minute quickstart (scripted flow for demos)
1) Clone minima-bootpack repo
2) Copy example.env -> .env and replace REDWOOD_API_KEY
3) Run: ./quickstart.sh or python quickstart.py
Expected output: a single JSON with text field and latency printed

quickstart.sh (shell):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
source .env
curl -s -X POST "$REDWOOD_API_URL" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"'$SAMPLE_MODEL'","input":"Write a two-sentence product blurb about a coffee mug"}' | jq .

quickstart.py (very small, stdlib only):
import os, json, urllib.request
API_URL = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_URL')
KEY = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
req = urllib.request.Request(API_URL, data=json.dumps({"model": os.getenv('SAMPLE_MODEL'), "input": "List three uses for a paperclip"}).encode(), headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}", "Content-Type": "application/json"})
resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req).read().decode()
print('response:', resp)

Runloop heuristics (how to keep iteration fast):
- Short feedback cycles: encourage devs to keep prompt+context under 300 tokens for iteration speed
- Local-first testing: provide a tiny local stub/mock server (mocks/echo) to avoid network throttles while iterating
- Deterministic seeds: include example deterministic params (temperature=0, top_p=0.7) for reproducible tests
- Incremental complexity: start with a single-turn generation, then add streaming and stateful KV cache usage

Telemetry & gating (minimal required signals):
- Success rate per route (200 vs 5xx)
- Median token latency and p95 token latency
- Cost per request (tokens * model-unit cost) as an approximation
- A small synthetic correctness test: a canonical prompt set with expected substrings (pass/fail)

Example telemetry contract (fields to emit)
- event_type: string (call.start | call.end | call.error)
- route: string (e.g., /api/chat)
- model: string
- latency_ms: number (end-start)
- tokens_in, tokens_out: number
- success: boolean
(note: these become labels in our console dashboards)

CI smoke tests (recommended minimal set):
- smoke/test_quickstart.sh: run the quickstart.sh with a valid dev token and assert HTTP 200 and a non-empty text field
- smoke/prompt_regression.py: run 5 canonical prompts and assert expected substrings; fail pipeline on >20% regression
- lint: docstring/README presence and example.env not containing real tokens

Observability hooks in sample code:
- a single function emit_event(name, payload) that calls a preapproved telemetry endpoint (or logs to stdout if local)
- attach request_id to logs and return it in response headers for debugging

Rollout advice for new SDK versions (safe defaults):
- default to backwards-compatible method signatures for one minor semver at minimum
- when shipping a signature change: provide an adapter shim in the SDK and a migration warning in logs
- Canary policy: enable new SDK for 5% of orgs/paths for 48 hours, monitor telemetry contract, then ramp over 7 days

Failure modes & recovery patterns:
- rate-limited calls: expose retry-with-backoff helper in examples (exponential backoff + jitter)
- transient model OOM/timeout: auto-fallback to smaller verified model with a warning token in response
- malformed input: SDK should return a clear error with hints (e.g., missing API key, invalid JSON)

Developer UX checklist (ship checklist for every quickstart update):
- [ ] One-command run path (or <3 commands) to get a response
- [ ] No installation beyond git + python/node/curl (prefer standard libs)
- [ ] Example env file and clear secret instructions
- [ ] CI smoke + prompt regression test added to tests/ci-smoke
- [ ] Telemetry hook present and documented
- [ ] Small note about data residency/security (link to private deployment doc)
- [ ] Accessibility: make sure examples are copy/paste friendly (no smart quotes)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want to include a tiny serverless/template (Vercel/Netlify) as a one-click deploy in the bootpack? Pros: lowers friction for demos. Cons: maintenance overhead and more moving parts. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketing-examples/pull/22)
- Should the minima bootpack include an ultra-cheap verified model recommendation list for regions (us-west, eu-west)? Need input from infra on region costs. (ENG-5872)
- UX experiment: try an inline onboarding modal in Console that injects the minima bootpack into a new org's workspace. Measure time-to-success.

Appendix: short sample guideline for docs authors
- Keep the first code block runnable within 60 seconds
- Put caveats and advanced options in a "Going further" section below the quickstart
- Keep prompt engineering guidance short and prescriptive (2–3 hints max)
- Link to relevant Console pages (tokens dashboard, model catalog)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally opinionated; aim to validate the 3/15/30 minute thresholds during the next SDK docs sprint.
- Suggested owners: Amina (playbook), Carlos (telemetry hooks), Priya (CI smoke), Jonah (packaging + one-click)

-- end of playbook --
